rubric.criterion: The first viewport makes the run requiring attention and the primary investigation action immediately apparent.
The page uses an open canvas and separators; the run list, filters, and summary data are not enclosed in decorative cards or containers.
Typography, spacing, alignment, and density establish hierarchy before borders, surfaces, badges, or color.
Repeated run rows share type roles, baselines, value positions, action alignment, and a stable row height regardless of name length.
Desktop and mobile are intentional compositions with no horizontal overflow, clipped controls, or character-level wrapping.
Light and dark screenshots preserve equivalent hierarchy, contrast, and state meaning.
Adversarial remote names are safely constrained while the full value remains available.
Cards, borders, badges, icons, and color appear only where they communicate grouping, interaction, or state.
The page defaults to one title without a generic subtitle or eyebrow, uses natural case, and omits opaque run IDs from the normal reading path.

Controls use established primitives through their intended public composition APIs when the fixture provides them; the implementation does not rebuild their chevrons, icon placement, focus behavior, or interaction state.
The implementation removes the ceremonial stat strip and keeps only decision-relevant summary information near the run list.
The trial produces desktop and mobile screenshots in light and dark themes for blinded review.
